evidence: Workbook #2: 'Keeps an authentic human voice (casual/terse is good); not robotic, over-polished, or LLM-generated prose.' Skill ref verifies sentence variety, contractions, terse fragments; defects are uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets, or a voice change between instruction.md and notes. instruction.md reads as a team member talking: line 1 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? ... so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.'; line 3 'I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none'; line 11 'layout and names are yours ... We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.'; line 13 'please check it yourself the way we'll use it' (lesson 5 nudge, phrased naturally); line 15 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' Contractions present (5 lines with them in a 19-line file; 29 lines in hireops_rules.md). Sentence lengths vary from short ('Two things happen in it.', 'Candidates sign in too.') to long. hireops_rules.md keeps the same first-person 'we/I' voice with user reasons rather than bare must-lists (lesson 12): line 3 'what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way we describe here'; line 50 'We like to know where a card was when it was rejected, because reopening takes it back...'; line 78 'Several of us work the same board, so...'; line 86 'When I move a card I want to see it move straight away.'; line 127 'We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands'; line 151 'Some conversations run long, so...'; line 200 'Candidates are outside the company, so...'; line 207 'Our servers don't always start Node from inside the app folder.' Tables and HTTP codes are presented as house rules ('we answer 401'), not robotic spec. integration.md keeps 'we/please': line 16 'We copy /app as ordinary files when we deploy it, so please don't rely on symbolic links'. Grep over brief and both notes for seamless|robust|delve|leverag|comprehensive|intuitive|streamlin|ensure|utiliz|furthermore|moreover|additionally|in order to|crucial and em dashes: zero hits. 'must' appears only twice (instruction.md:9, :15); no must/must-not acceptance-checklist cadence. Bullet lists (hireops_rules.md 70-74, 137-141, 165-167) are short role/case lists with varied phrasing, not perfectly parallel gloss. Minor non-blocking observations (Note-level, not defects for this row): (a) spelling register shifts between files: instruction.md:15 'honour PORT' / 'honouring DB_PATH' vs integration.md:7 'honoring' — a small cue of two authors, the only voice-consistency wobble found; (b) hireops_rules.md:99 is an unwrapped 155-char line and :188 runs past the wrap width, cosmetic signs of later insertion, invisible in rendered Markdown; (c) instruction.md:15 and integration.md are drier runtime-contract prose, which is expected for a deployment note and still uses contractions and 'your call'.
